A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 32 pages of v2 and 40 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison; retained proofs, experiments, and relocated figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original synthetic, CIFAR-10, and Fashion-MNIST experiments. Appendices B.3 and D.1–D.2 contain additional simulations and corruption analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds NLP and peer-review estimates, FeeBee evaluations in Tables 1–2, and order-breakage experiments in Appendix D.5.

M1.justification: The proposed estimator still sorts corrupted soft labels, fits isotonic least squares using hard labels, and averages the minimum calibrated class probabilities. The additional calibrators are evaluated alternatives; the proposed procedure and hard-label estimator are unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 retains the synthetic and image datasets and adds ChaosNLI's SNLI, MNLI, and AbductiveNLI datasets, plus pooled and annual ICLR 2017–2025 peer-review datasets. FeeBee label-noise injection and non-order-preserving corruption also introduce distinct testing conditions.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds evaluated Platt scaling and three restricted beta-calibration variants: beta-am, beta-ab, and beta-a. Platt scaling was previously discussed but not evaluated. Appendix D.3.2 clarifies that the existing beta comparator was already the full three-parameter version, so that baseline is retained.

E3.justification: The new FeeBee protocol uses 101 noise levels, a penalty against noise-dependent Bayes-error bounds, and histogram-bin counts from 10 to n/2 in increments of five. Appendix D.5 adds a Gaussian logit-noise sweep with and without averaging 50 hard labels. The previously reported synthetic/image settings and ResNet training budget are retained.

E4.justification: The existing bias and corruption analyses remain. Appendix D.5 adds controlled violations of order preservation, quantified through Kendall tau, with and without additional binomial noise. FeeBee additionally examines responses to injected label noise and sensitivity to histogram-bin selection.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 bootstrap resamples, 95% bootstrap intervals, and 1,000 repetitions for Appendix B.3. v3 newly identifies the synthetic bootstrap display as BCa in Figure 11a. This adds statistical disclosure without establishing a change in resampling procedure or run counts.

E6.justification: v3 adds NLP/peer-review estimates and FeeBee results; isotonic ranks first throughout Tables 1–2, including CIFAR-10 scores of 0.1131 versus 0.1701 for beta. Figure 12 newly shows degradation with order breakage and persistent beta-family errors with additional noise. Figure 4a also updates synthetic estimates: isotonic changes from approximately 8.01% to 7.68%. The clean-reference estimate also changes, so this does not establish a method improvement.

T1.justification: The corruption-function domain is corrected from a >= 0 to a > 0 in Section 4.1 and Appendix D.1, excluding the undefined 1/a case. Appendix D.4.1 adds FeeBee's noise/Bayes-error relationship and associated bounds. The main theorems, corollaries, and proofs in Appendices B–C are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraphs, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: separation-adaptive bias bounds and instance-free estimation through isotonic calibration under ordering assumptions. The expanded experimental evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 leaves stronger assessment of real-world estimates as future work. v3 argues that FeeBee supplies a practical comparison and supports choosing isotonic calibration. Appendix D.5 adds empirical qualifications concerning ordering violations and noise. The new peer-review application also interprets estimates based on acceptance decisions as inherent reviewing difficulty.

D1.justification: v3 adds ICLR data-construction instructions, beta-variant constraints, FeeBee implementation choices, and the order-breakage generator. A reproducibility statement identifies supplementary code and README instructions; the original repository link, library versions, and hardware details remain. One new detail is ambiguous: Appendix D.4.2 names ViT reference errors for Fashion-MNIST, whereas Section 4.1 and the retained training description specify ResNet-18.

R1.justification: v3 adds Nie et al. (2020), Zhou et al. (2022), and Kendall (1938), and expands the role of the already-cited Renggli et al. (2021) through FeeBee. Appendix A and the central positioning relative to Ishida et al. and isotonic-regression research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 gains dataset-specific paragraphs and separates Bayes-error estimation from FeeBee comparison. v3 adds experimental subsections, acknowledgments, reproducibility and LLM-use statements, and localized terminology, typo, affiliation, and publication-header edits. The broader narrative and theoretical exposition are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from horizontal to vertical bars and accommodates additional comparators. New Tables 1–2 display FeeBee results; Figure 11 repeats Figure 4 alongside additional datasets, and Figure 12 presents order-breakage curves. These substantially expand the experimental displays while retaining the earlier appendix figures.

improvement.justification: v2 acknowledged weak validation of real-world estimates and left better assessment to future work. v3's FeeBee comparisons and controlled order-breakage tests substantially strengthen the empirical justification for isotonic calibration and clarify its practical limits. These gains outweigh the localized Fashion-MNIST reference inconsistency, although FeeBee remains an indirect validation and does not identify the true Bayes errors.
